key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 treatment initially reduces ETL/perovskite interfacial recombination, but thermal aging drives faster degradation extending into the absorber.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive, nondestructive monitoring can help engineers evaluate whether interface passivation improves both initial performance and thermal durability.
method: Use multiple excitation wavelengths to probe depth-dependent photoluminescence decay.
Track recombination changes in PEABF4-treated perovskite stacks during thermal aging.
Interpret decay signatures with diffusion–recombination simulations.
evidence_signal: PL measurements indicate reduced recombination losses from fullerene deposition after treatment, followed by faster degradation during thermal aging; simulations support interface-versus-bulk interpretations.
watch_item: Depth attribution is model-supported rather than direct, and the abstract provides no quantitative lifetime or device-efficiency benchmarks.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
